reason: The text portrays the majority of the elite scouts (the princes and leaders of Israel selected to spy out Canaan) strongly unfavorably. The ten scouts who gave a negative report are explicitly condemned—they spread a 'bad report' (דִּבַּת־הָאָרֶץ רָעָה) that discouraged the Israelites, and God punishes them with death (וַיָּמֻתוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים מוֹצִאֵי דִבַּת־הָאָרֶץ רָעָה בַּמַּגֵּפָה). They are contrasted sharply with the few elite figures (Joshua and Caleb) who maintain faith and are portrayed positively. The broader narrative also presents the congregation's leadership as failing in faith. However, not all elite are portrayed unfavorably—Joshua, Caleb, Moses, and Aaron show faithfulness.
